title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
seo_title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 3)
standard_code: Class 10, Chapter 3: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
standard_text: Pair of linear equations in two variables and graphical method of their solution; consistency/inconsistency; algebraic conditions for number of solutions; solution by substitution and by elimination; simple situational problems (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Pair of Linear Equations worksheet (NCERT Chapter 3): graphs, consistency, substitution, elimination and word problems in rupees. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Two lines: intersect, coincide or are parallel
key_sub: One solution, infinitely many, or none.
body_html:
How it works

A pair a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0, a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 is shown by two lines. The solution is their point of intersection.

a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂: one solution (intersecting). a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂: infinitely many (coincident). a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂: none (parallel).

Substitution: make one variable the subject and put it into the other equation. Elimination: make the coefficients of one variable equal, then add or subtract.

Example

Solve x + y = 14, x − y = 4.

Add: 2x = 18, so x = 9

Then y = 14 − 9 = 5

Answer: x = 9, y = 5

Example

Do 2x + 3y = 9 and 4x + 6y = 18 have a solution?

2/4 = 3/6 = 9/18 = ½

Answer: Infinitely many (coincident lines)

Common mistakes

  • Swapping the values of x and y at the end.
  • Calling parallel lines “infinitely many solutions”. Parallel lines never meet: no solution.
  • Stopping after finding x. Substitute back to find y too.

faq.q: How do I know if a pair of linear equations has a unique solution?
faq.a: Compare the ratios: if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, the lines intersect at one point, so there is a unique solution.

faq.q: When does a pair of linear equations have no solution?
faq.a: When a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂. The lines are parallel and never meet. Such a pair is called inconsistent.
Multiply the equations so that one variable has the same coefficient, then add or subtract to remove it and solve for the other.

faq.q: Which method is best: substitution or elimination?
faq.a: Use substitution when one variable already has coefficient 1; otherwise elimination is usually quicker.

items.q:
Which point (x, y) is the solution of the pair
4x + 2y = −6
−3x + 4y = 10 ?
items.e: Substitute into both equations: 4(−2) + 2(1) = −6 and −3(−2) + 4(1) = 10 are both true for (−2, 1).
The solution is the point where the two lines intersect: (2, −1), so x = 2, y = −1.
The solution is the point where the two lines intersect: (−2, −1), so x = −2, y = −1.
The solution is the point where the two lines intersect: (−3, −2), so x = −3, y = −2.

items.q:

−x − y = −2 ?
items.e: Substitute into both equations: −2(−1) − 4(3) = −10 and −(−1) − (3) = −2 are both true for (−1, 3).
The solution is the point where the two lines intersect: (3, −2), so x = 3, y = −2.

items.q:

items.e: Substitute into both equations: −4(4) + 3(−3) = −25 and 2(4) + 2(−3) = 2 are both true for (4, −3).
The solution is the point where the two lines intersect: (3, 2), so x = 3, y = 2.

items.e: Substitute into both equations: −2(−4) + 2(−3) = 2 and 3(−4) + (−3) = −15 are both true for (−4, −3).

items.q:

items.e: Substitute into both equations: 2(−2) + 5(−5) = −29 and 4(−2) + 5(−5) = −33 are both true for (−2, −5).
The solution is the point where the two lines intersect: (−1, 3), so x = −1, y = 3.

items.q:

items.e: Substitute into both equations: −3(−1) + 2(2) = 7 and −3(−1) + 3(2) = 9 are both true for (−1, 2).
The solution is the point where the two lines intersect: (1, 2), so x = 1, y = 2.

items.q: 1 pen and 3 pencils cost ₹30. 3 pens and 6 pencils cost ₹81. Find the cost of one pen and one pencil.
items.e: Let one pen cost ₹x and one pencil cost ₹y: x + 3y = 30 and 3x + 6y = 81. Solving gives ₹21 and ₹3.

items.q: A taxi charges a fixed amount plus a charge per km. For 20 km the fare is ₹300 and for 12 km it is ₹188. What is the fixed charge?
items.e: x + 20y = 300 and x + 12y = 188. Subtract: y = ₹14 per km, so fixed charge ₹20.

items.q: A fraction becomes 710 if 2 is added to both the numerator and the denominator, and 12 if 2 is subtracted from both. Find the fraction.

items.q: The perimeter of a rectangular garden is 32 m and its length is 2 m more than its width. Find the length and the width.

items.q: A library charges a fixed fee for the first 3 days and an extra charge for each day after that. Nikhil paid ₹37 for a book kept 9 days and ₹41 for 11 days. What is the charge for each extra day?

items.q: 3 chairs and 4 stools cost ₹3,710. 4 chairs and 5 stools cost ₹4,835. Find the cost of one chair and one stool.
items.e: Let one chair cost ₹x and one stool cost ₹y: 3x + 4y = 3,710 and 4x + 5y = 4,835. Solving gives ₹790 and ₹335.

items.q: Shreya has 17 notes of ₹10 and ₹20 worth ₹240 in all. How many ₹10 notes does she have?
items.e: x + y = 17 and 10x + 20y = 240. Solving gives 10 notes of ₹10.

items.q: A fraction becomes 12 if 1 is added to both the numerator and the denominator, and 13 if 2 is subtracted from both. Find the fraction.
items.e: Let it be x/y: (x + 1)/(y + 1) = 12 and (x − 2)/(y − 2) = 13. Solving gives 5/11.

items.q: A fraction becomes 1113 if 2 is added to both the numerator and the denominator, and 34 if 3 is subtracted from both. Find the fraction.
items.e: Let it be x/y: (x + 2)/(y + 2) = 1113 and (x − 3)/(y − 3) = 34. Solving gives 9/11.
